items.q: Statement 1: 'Total revenue = Total costs + profit.' Statement 2: 'Total contribution = (Contribution per unit x quantity) + fixed costs.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 is true: TR = TC + Profit (rearranged from Profit = TR - TC). Statement 2 is false: Total contribution = CPU x quantity. It does not include fixed costs. The correct formula with FC would be: Total Revenue = Total Contribution + Fixed Costs. Statement 2 confuses total contribution with total revenue. Total contribution = CPU x Q.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Which one of the following is not an extension strategy?
opts: Attracting new market segments
Changing the image of a product
Increasing spending on promotions
Lowering unit costs
items.why: Lowering unit costs is a cost reduction strategy, not an extension strategy. Extension strategies aim to extend the product life cycle by boosting sales: new segments, rebranding, more promotions. Extension strategies = extending sales/demand. Lowering costs improves profitability but doesn't directly boost sales.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Nexgen Software restructures its development teams so that each team sets its own sprint goals, allocates tasks internally, and decides how to solve technical problems without manager approval. Which non-financial motivation method does this most closely represent?
opts: Job rotation
Flexible working
Empowerment
Performance-related pay
items.why: Empowerment gives employees the authority and autonomy to make decisions about their own work. The scenario describes teams controlling goal-setting, task allocation, and problem-solving — all hallmarks of empowerment. Flexible working relates to when or where work is done, not decision-making authority. Performance-related pay is a financial method.
items.label: New question

items.q: Debt factoring is when:
opts: An organisation buys the right to collect money from credit sales of a business
An organisation estimates the value of its debts
Suppliers allow credit terms
The current ratio shows low liquidity
items.why: Debt factoring means a specialist company (the factor) purchases the right to collect a business's receivables, giving the business immediate cash (at a discount). Debt factoring is about selling your receivables to get cash now. The factor takes on the risk and collection.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Statement 1: 'An increase in rent paid by a business will have no effect on its gross profit.' Statement 2: 'An increase in tax on a business's profit will have no effect on its profit for the year.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 is true - gross profit = revenue minus cost of sales. Rent is an overhead deducted after gross profit. Statement 2 is false - tax directly reduces profit for the year. Many students confuse gross profit with operating/net profit. Gross profit only considers revenue and cost of sales (direct costs).
items.label: Past paper question

items.q:
Statement 1: Herzberg argued that improving hygiene factors such as salary will motivate workers in the long run.

Statement 2: Herzberg's two-factor theory suggests that job enrichment is a more effective long-term motivator than increasing basic pay.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 is false: Herzberg stated that hygiene factors (including salary) can only prevent dissatisfaction; they cannot positively motivate. Statement 2 is true: job enrichment is a direct application of Herzberg's motivators — it adds responsibility, challenge, and achievement to a role, which Herzberg identified as genuine sources of motivation.
items.label: New question

items.q: Table shows 4 scenarios of interest rate and wage changes. Which encourages switch from labour-intensive to capital-intensive?
opts: Scenario A (rates up, wages up)
Scenario B (rates up, wages down)
Scenario C (rates down, wages up)
Scenario D (rates down, wages down)
items.why: Lower interest rates make borrowing for machinery cheaper. Higher wages make labour more expensive. Both factors push towards replacing workers with capital equipment. Lower rates = cheaper capital. Higher wages = more expensive labour.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Statement 1: 'TR - profit = Total contribution + FC.' Statement 2: '(SP x Q) - FC = Profit + variable costs.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1: TR - Profit = TC (total costs). But Total contribution + FC is not TC; TC = TVC + FC. So Statement 1 is false. Statement 2: (SP x Q) - FC = TR - FC. And Profit + VC = (TR - TC) + TVC = TR - FC. So Statement 2 is true. These formula manipulation questions require careful algebraic thinking. Write out each side and simplify.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q:
Statement 1: Job rotation and job enrichment both increase the level of responsibility and decision-making authority given to an employee.

Statement 2: Job enrichment is more closely aligned with Herzberg's motivators than job rotation is.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 is false: job rotation moves workers between tasks of similar complexity to reduce repetition but does not increase responsibility. Job enrichment specifically extends the depth of a role by adding greater responsibility and autonomy. Statement 2 is true: job enrichment directly targets Herzberg's motivators (responsibility, achievement, the work itself), whereas rotation mainly addresses boredom without adding genuine motivators.
items.label: New question

items.q:
Statement 1: Employee engagement refers solely to the level of job satisfaction reported by employees in an annual survey.

Statement 2: High levels of employee engagement are associated with lower labour turnover and higher productivity.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 is false: employee engagement is broader than satisfaction — it encompasses emotional commitment to the organisation's goals, willingness to go beyond minimum requirements, and a sense of purpose in one's role. Statement 2 is true: engaged employees are more likely to remain with the business and to put in discretionary effort, raising productivity.
items.label: New question

items.q: Three changes: 1) Reduction in wages. 2) Increase in labour productivity. 3) Increase in labour turnover. Which leads to increased employee costs as % of turnover?
opts: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
2 only
3 only
items.why: Lower wages (1) reduce employee costs. Higher productivity (2) means more output per worker, spreading costs over more units. Only increased turnover (3) raises employee costs (recruitment, training costs for replacements) without increasing revenue. Higher turnover = more recruitment/training costs = higher employee costs as a % of revenue. Wage cuts and productivity gains both reduce this ratio.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Hartwell Manufacturing introduces time-and-motion studies to find the single best way to complete each assembly task. Workers are paid piece rate based on output. Which statement best explains why Taylor believed this approach would maximise productivity?
opts: Workers are primarily motivated by social belonging and will work harder when placed in cohesive team structures where peer pressure encourages consistent output levels.
Workers are primarily motivated by money and will respond to clear targets linked to financial reward.
Workers are intrinsically motivated and need autonomy to find their own most efficient methods, so managerial interference reduces overall productivity.
Workers are motivated by recognition, so publicising output data and ranking individuals against one another increases discretionary effort across the workforce.
items.why: Taylor's scientific management rests on the assumption that workers are rational economic agents motivated above all by pay. Linking piece rate to a scientifically determined best method removes inefficiency and directly rewards output. The social-belonging answer reflects Mayo, not Taylor, and autonomy is the opposite of Taylor's centralised, manager-directed approach.
items.label: New question

items.q: A manager wants to motivate someone who has satisfied esteem needs. Focus on:
opts: Physiological needs
Security needs
Self-actualisation needs
Social needs
items.why: According to Maslow, once esteem needs are met, the next level up is self-actualisation (reaching full potential, creativity, personal growth). You always motivate with the next unsatisfied level. Maslow's hierarchy goes up. If esteem is satisfied, the next need is self-actualisation at the top.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Calloway Foods employs both production-line workers paid per unit produced and office managers who receive a bonus if annual targets are met. Which row correctly identifies the financial motivation method used for each group?
opts: Production workers: commission; managers: piece rate
Production workers: piece rate; managers: performance-related pay
Production workers: performance-related pay; managers: commission
Production workers: piece rate; managers: commission
items.why: Piece rate pays a set amount per unit of output and is typical in manufacturing. Performance-related pay (PRP) awards a bonus linked to assessed performance against targets and is common for managerial roles. Commission is specifically linked to sales revenue generated, which does not apply to either group described here.
items.label: New question

items.q: According to Herzberg, which of the following is correctly classified as a motivator rather than a hygiene factor?
opts: Company policy and administration
Quality of supervision
Achievement and recognition
Working conditions
items.why: Herzberg's motivators are intrinsic to the work itself and include achievement, recognition, responsibility, advancement, and the work itself. Company policy, supervision quality, and working conditions are all hygiene factors — their absence causes dissatisfaction but their presence does not in itself motivate. Students frequently confuse recognition with a hygiene factor because it feels like an external reward.
items.label: New question

items.q: According to Lewin's force field analysis:
opts: Change occurs if driving forces are stronger than restraining forces
Change occurs if negative forces equal positive forces
A company grows if S&O outweigh W&T
A company grows if horizontal and vertical forces balance
items.why: Lewin's force field analysis states that change happens when driving forces (pushing for change) overcome restraining forces (resisting change). If they're equal, the status quo remains. C describes SWOT analysis, not Lewin. D is nonsensical.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q:
Statement 1: A sole trader and the business they own are treated as the same legal entity.
Statement 2: A private limited company is a separate legal entity from its shareholders.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Both statements are true. A sole trader has no legal separation between themselves and their business, which is why they face unlimited liability. A limited company has its own legal identity — it can sue, be sued, and own assets in its own name, separately from its shareholders. This distinction underpins the concept of limited liability.
items.label: New question

items.q: Table shows scenarios of managers' willingness to change vs likelihood of external changes. Strategic drift is LEAST likely in:
opts: Scenario A (High willingness, High external change)
Scenario B (High willingness, Low external change)
Scenario C (Low willingness, High external change)
Scenario D (Low willingness, Low external change)
items.why: Strategic drift occurs when a business doesn't adapt to change. If managers are highly willing to change and external changes are low (less to adapt to), drift is least likely. High willingness handles whatever small changes occur. Worst case for drift: low willingness + high change (C). Best case: high willingness + low change (B).
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Grania's Gym operates in a town where three other gyms compete for the same customers. Many members switch gym each time their contract expires. According to Porter's five forces, which combination of forces is most directly reflected in this situation?
opts: High threat of new entrants and high supplier power
High competitive rivalry and high buyer power
High threat of substitutes and low competitive rivalry
Low buyer power and high competitive rivalry
items.why: Three existing competitors fighting for the same customers represents high competitive rivalry. Members who regularly switch suppliers are exercising high buyer power. Students often confuse buyer power (the ability of customers to switch or negotiate) with the threat of substitutes (alternative product types).
items.label: New question

items.q:
Statement 1: According to Maslow, a worker whose job is at risk of redundancy will be primarily motivated by opportunities for promotion and self-development.

Statement 2: Maslow's hierarchy implies that offering a pay rise will have little motivational effect on an employee whose physiological and safety needs are already met.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 is false: a threat of redundancy threatens safety needs, so the worker will be focused on that lower level, not self-actualisation. Statement 2 is true: Maslow argues that a satisfied need ceases to motivate, so if lower-order needs are met, pay (which addresses those lower levels) will have diminishing motivational power compared with higher-order factors.
items.label: New question
